title: Eurovision to bar countries at war from hosting: What that means
facts: The European Broadcasting Union announced that countries involved in armed conflict will be barred from hosting the Eurovision Song Contest.
The European Broadcasting Union was established in 1956 and organizes the annual Eurovision Song Contest.
Bulgaria won the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest and was designated host for the 2027 event.
Ukraine won Eurovision in 2022 but was unable to host the 2023 edition due to war with Russia.
The United Kingdom hosted the 2023 Eurovision Song Contest on behalf of Ukraine.
Israel became the first non-European country to participate in the Eurovision Song Contest in 1973.
The European Broadcasting Union will commission independent security assessments if a winning country faces geopolitical instability.
Martin Green serves as director of the Eurovision Song Contest.
Public broadcasters from the Netherlands, Slovenia, Spain, Iceland, and Ireland boycotted the 2026 contest over Israel's inclusion.
AVROTROS is the Dutch public broadcaster that boycotted the 2026 Eurovision contest.
Alfonso Morales serves as secretary-general of Spanish public broadcaster RTVE.
Stefan Eiriksson serves as Director-General of Icelandic public broadcaster RUV.
Thirty-five countries participated in the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna.
Israel finished in second place in the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest.
Sven Kuhn von Burgsdorff previously served as European Union representative to the occupied West Bank and Gaza.
